title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a case of an automated alert being treated as an identification. License plate cameras flagged a stolen Camaro, and an undercover unit reported a car that matched. The deputies and the helicopter could not read the plates on the car in front of them, so the one piece of evidence that would have confirmed or ruled out the match was never obtained. The stop went ahead on the strength of the alert and the visual match alone.

The failure sits at the handoff between a camera system's output and the officers who act on it. A flag from a plate camera identifies a plate, not a car, and it does not transfer to a vehicle whose plate has not been read. Catching this would have required a positive plate read before the stop, or a decision to hold back when the plate could not be read. Instead the response escalated to at least five patrol cars, a helicopter, drawn guns and handcuffs, and the error was recognised only after the men were restrained.

What is not established is whether the deputy pushed Julian to the ground or threatened to shoot him, which rests on the men's account, and whether any procedure was breached, which supervisors are still reviewing from body worn camera footage. The internal affairs complaints have been planned, not resolved, and no finding has been made against the deputies.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in Cypress, Texas, Harris County sheriff's deputies mistook two men, both 19, Anthony and Julian, for suspects in a stolen Camaro. Deputies surrounded Anthony's car with at least five patrol cars and a helicopter, pointed guns, and handcuffed them. Julian said a deputy pushed him to the ground and threatened to shoot and kill him, and he showed cuts and scrapes. The men were not suspects and faced no charges.

The sheriff's office said license plate cameras had flagged a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies. An undercover unit saw a matching car, but deputies and the helicopter could not read its plates, so backup was called. After handcuffing the men, deputies realized it was the wrong car. Anthony's mother, Leslie, wants accountability and plans to hire an attorney. Supervisors will review body worn camera footage for proper procedures, and both men plan to file formal complaints with internal affairs.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
